name: Shunat Nimrin, road junction
position_source: CORONA DF041 d registered to HEXAGON A017e (43 blocks, 11 m)
note: Same roads and walled compound in 1967 and 1974

name: Suwwan
type: rubble mound on a spur (possible building)
position_source: image, tile A017e (1 Dec 1974), Kafrein transform
note: Dark speckled patch approximately 25 by 30 m on a spur top between two gullies. Agrees in size and ground form with 17 APAAME photographs of 28 Oct 2014 (title Suwwan; Flickr list position 231 m away). CORONA 1967 too light. No straight sides visible. No EAMENA record within 500 m Second image: HEXAGON A014c of June 1974, registered to the elevation model (25 blocks, 30 m), shows a group of dark spots at the east end of the same gully, at the same place to approximately 30 m. Checked for the presence of the stone patch on two images; no building form is visible.

name: Karama Ruin 5 (Ain al-Heri)
type: building of two parts on a spur
position_source: image, tile A017e (1 Dec 1974), window registered to the elevation model (155 blocks, 12 m)
note: Two joined rectangles with dark wall lines, approximately 22 by 36 m and 36 by 24 m, on a flat spur top above a gorge with vegetation. Same form on APAAME photographs of 24 Sep 2017 (title Karama Ruin 5 / Heri / Ain al-Heri; Flickr list position 137 m away). No EAMENA record within 500 m Second image: HEXAGON A015c of June 1974 shows the same two joined rectangles.

name: el-Heri Tower
position_source: image, tile A017e (1 Dec 1974), window registered to the elevation model (155 blocks, 12 m)
note: One oval ring approximately 10 m across on open ground south of a small wadi. APAAME photographs of 24 Sep 2017 show a small round stone structure on a plateau (Flickr list position 104 m away). No EAMENA record within 500 m Second image: HEXAGON A015c of June 1974 shows the same ring.

name: Karama Ruins 14
position_source: image, tile A017e (1 Dec 1974), window registered to the elevation model (155 blocks, 12 m)
note: Round feature approximately 11 m across on a field plateau north of a gorge. APAAME photographs of 24 Sep 2017 show a ring of stones on a ploughed plateau near a gorge edge, with two small rectangular enclosures near it (Flickr list position 199 m away). No EAMENA record within 500 m HEXAGON A015c of June 1974 shows a faint light patch with one dark spot at the same place (weak). Second exposure: HEXAGON F017c (forward camera, 1 Dec 1974) shows the same round light feature with the same shadow and inner spot (block match 0.87). Checked on two exposures of the same day; June 1974 is weak.

name: Karama Ruins 16
position_source: image, tile A017e (1 Dec 1974), window registered to the elevation model (79 blocks, 10 m)
note: Round light feature approximately 18 m across on a small flat-topped knoll above a scarp. APAAME photographs of 24 Sep 2017 show a ring on a flat-topped knoll above a scarp, and more rings on the plateau near it (Flickr list position 263 m away). No EAMENA record within 500 m Second image: HEXAGON F007d of 5 May 1978 shows the same knoll with a ring wall, clearer than in 1974.

name: ʿAin Duk, head of the spring gardens
position_source: images F016b (1 Dec 1974) and F006c (5 May 1978), each linked to a registered frame through the frame overlap (51 and 11 blocks)
note: Trees and a small structure where the irrigated plots start, at the foot of the scarp; the two dates agree to 15 m. The water is not visible. EAMENA record: EAMENA-0117143 (3 m). The entry table uses this point from 11 Nov 2026; its old point (PEF sheet XVIII, georeferenced) is 415 m to the west-north-west on a bare slope.

name: Tell el-Qos (published point)
type: tell in the built-up area of Jericho
position_source: EAMENA-0117188; point shown on images F017b (1 Dec 1974) and F007c (5 May 1978)
note: Open light ground approximately 60 m across on the north bank of Wadi Qelt in 1974; houses on a part of it in 1978. No mound shape can be read between the houses and trees. The entry table uses this point from 11 Nov 2026; its old point (PEF sheet XVIII, georeferenced) is 165 m to the north in an orchard with houses.

name: Dome of the Rock (control for the Jerusalem window)
position_source: published coordinate; the Jerusalem window of F017b is registered to the elevation model (141 blocks, 18 m with a height term) and then moved 48 m to put this point right
note: With this one control, nine other landmarks with published coordinates (gates of the Old City, al-Aqsa, Holy Sepulchre, Church of All Nations) are at their places on the image, to approximately 30 m. The image of 5 May 1978 (F007c) is registered independently (30 blocks, 7 m with a height term; moved 19 m to this point): the same nine landmarks are at their places.

name: Tell el-Ful, structure on the summit
position_source: image, tile F017b (1 Dec 1974), Jerusalem window
note: Terraced hill with a rectangular structure on the top. The entry-table point (Pleiades 749935552) is 8 m away. On the image of 5 May 1978 the point is approximately 35 m east of the centre of the large building on the summit.

name: Machaerus, rectangle north-west of the citadel
type: rectangular enclosure with rounded corners (probable Roman siege camp)
position_source: image, tile F018c (1 Dec 1974), Machaerus transform with height term
note: Double line, approximately 65 m by 30 m, at the edge of a ridge above the wadi, 460 m west-north-west of the citadel summit. Also on the image of 25 June 1974 (aft camera, tile A016c): the same rectangle at the same place relative to the citadel. The camp letter of the published siege plan is not assigned. South of the scroll region.

name: Machaerus, rectangle south-west of the citadel
type: rectangular enclosure with rounded corners (probable Roman siege camp)
position_source: image, tile F018c (1 Dec 1974), Machaerus transform with height term
note: Double line, approximately 44 m by 30 m, at the edge of a ridge above the wadi, 550 m west-south-west of the citadel summit. Also on the image of 25 June 1974 (aft camera, tile A016c): the same rectangle at the same place relative to the citadel. The camp letter of the published siege plan is not assigned. South of the scroll region.

name: Mount Gerizim, octagonal church of Mary Theotokos
position_source: coordinate of the CORPS database (ITM 225.95 / 678.48); identified on tile F014a (1 Dec 1974) and on a modern image
note: Octagon with concentric rings inside a rectangular enclosure. Inner ring approximately 30 m; enclosure approximately 75 m west to east (database: church 30 by 37.4 m, enclosure 71 by 56 m). The registration to the elevation model puts it 166 m away (height effect at the summit); used as control point. Entry 57 place: table point 110 m north.

name: Mount Gerizim, monumental eastern staircase (plan part 34)
position_source: general plan of the precinct (Magen 2008, JSP 8, Fig. 14) fitted to a modern image of 29 Oct 2026 with five control points; position relative to the church
note: Two or three parallel east-west lines, approximately 30 m long and 18 to 20 m apart, inside the plan outline (plan: approximately 21 by 31 m; report: up to 23 by 34 m). Single steps are not visible. Excavated after 1982; not visible in 1974. Entry 57 has 'the steps'; this is a position for a feature of that kind, not evidence for the entry.

name: Mount Gerizim, enclosure on the northern spur
type: walled enclosure in a forest clearing
position_source: image, tile F014a (1 Dec 1974), with the control point at the church
note: Approximately 100 m across, 560 m north-north-east of the entry table point, above Nablus. Probable: Tell er-Ras. Not compared with the plans of Bull 1967 and 1968.

name: Beth Shean, mound (Tell el-Husn), summit
position_source: image, tile b of frame D3C1209-200214F012 (1 Dec 1974), registered to the elevation model (local residual 18 m)
note: Oval mound approximately 250 by 200 m above the bend of Nahal Harod; trenches on the summit. Also on tile d of frame D3C1208-400636F009 (25 Jun 1974), linked to the December image. Entry 58 place: table point on the mound, 60 m from the summit centre. Nahal Harod north of the mound checked with the site plan of NEAEHL vol. 5 p. 1624.

name: Beth Shean, Roman theatre
position_source: image, tile b of frame D3C1209-200214F012 (1 Dec 1974)
note: Semicircular structure 300 m south-south-west of the mound; agrees with the site plan of NEAEHL vol. 5 p. 1624. Also on the image of 25 Jun 1974.

name: Kh. Ibziq, oval mound with buildings
type: mound with a wall or terrace line
position_source: image, tile F013c (1 Dec 1974), registered to the elevation model (residual 40 m), no control point
note: Approximately 170 m across, three or four standing buildings on its west side; a field of small walled cells 230 m east-south-east. 80 m from the entry table point (entry 59, possible). Which of the two survey ruins (Upper, Lower) this is, is not known.

name: Beth Shean, ʿAin el-Melʿab (spring at the theatre)
position_source: Plan of Beisan of the Survey of Western Palestine (Conder and Kitchener 1882, after p. 104; reproduced in Mazor and Najjar 2007, Fig. 1.1), placed relative to the theatre on tile b of frame D3C1209-200214F012
note: The plan of 1882 marks a spring ʿAin el-Melʿab at the east end of the theatre, with a stream to the north. On the images of 1 Dec 1974 and 25 Jun 1974, a dense group of trees is at this position; the spring is not visible. Entry 58 has 'the mouth of the spring'; this is a candidate position, not evidence for the entry. The plan also marks ʿAin el-Malhah 250 m south-west and ʿAin et-Tineh at the north-east bridge.

name: Qumran, straight line on the plateau (aqueduct channel line)
position_source: Plan of the Qumran aqueduct (Ilan and Amit 1989, fig. 1), fitted to tile F007c (5 May 1978) with one anchor, scale from the bar; position relative to the ruin
note: Straight light line approximately 270 m long from the cliff top to the north-west of the ruin; plan points 16 to 18 are on it to approximately 5 m. Also visible on the image of 1 Dec 1974. A path or a fence on the channel line can give the same picture. NEAEHL vol. 4 p. 1237 has the entrance of the aqueduct at the north-west corner of the ruin. Entry 21 has 'the head of the water conduit'; this is not evidence for the entry.

name: Qumran aqueduct, basin below the waterfall (plan point 2)
type: aqueduct basin (position from a plan of 1989)
position_source: Plan of the Qumran aqueduct (Ilan and Amit 1989, fig. 1), fitted to tile F007c (5 May 1978) with one anchor; 412 m west and 24 m south of the centre of the ruin
note: Inside the gorge: rock and shadow on the image. The basin is not visible. Candidate A for the head of the conduit of entry 21; candidate C is the channel entrance at the north-west corner of the ruin (31.7412 N, 35.4594 E). The image cannot decide between them.
